title: The Escalation Exit Note
subtitle: Before an account escalation changes status
intro_text: Use this in the existing escalation record with the account lead and the people who own the fix. The customer-facing update should agree with this note. Do not put customer names or private details in a public copy.

example.heading: Example: service restored, adoption still blocked
example.label: Fictional example, not a customer result.
example.interpretation: The support incident may be resolved. The account escalation stays open until the customer can verify the affected workflow or accepts a named handoff.

sections.title: What changed for the customer?
sections.instruction: Write the original customer impact and the evidence that it ended. Record what the customer has verified and what remains unknown.

sections.title: What remains open?
sections.instruction: Separate the urgent impact from cleanup, workaround, product decision or account plan. Give each open item an owner and next date.

sections.title: Choose the status
sections.instruction: Close only if the exit test is met and the customer understands the outcome. Handoff if urgent impact ended but named work remains. Keep open if the impact or decision is still unresolved.

prompt:
Original customer impact: [ ]
Evidence it ended: [ ]
Customer confirmation or stated disagreement: [ ]
Open work, owner and date: [ ]
Choice: close / handoff / keep open [ ]
Next customer update: [owner, channel, date]
next_action: Use on one live escalation before changing its status. Keep the note in the existing case, not a new dashboard.
methodology: An original editorial decision aid informed by public GitLab, Atlassian and Google operating guidance. It is not a measured retention intervention or a substitute for contractual incident obligations.
